subject.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)

question: Should OpenClaw expose `capabilities.tts.voice.captionedFinalText` as a supported channel-plugin contract that permits core to defer normally visible final-mode TTS text?
rationale: This is a public plugin-facing behavior contract with message-delivery consequences; source review can assess its mechanics but cannot choose the permanent API and compatibility direction.

options.title: Approve the generic capability contract
options.body: Retain the capability, require focused current-head Telegram proof and compatibility tests, and treat caption support as an explicit plugin opt-in.

options.title: Keep the behavior Telegram-owned
options.body: Avoid adding the public capability for now and move any Telegram-specific delivery policy into the Telegram owner boundary until a broader SDK contract is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic capability contract
recommendation.body: Retain the capability, require focused current-head Telegram proof and compatibility tests, and treat caption support as an explicit plugin opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: The visible timeline shows direct engagement with this PR; no stronger feature-history owner could be established from the read-only review context.
